source.version_note: International Journal of Social Robotics18:75, published online19June2026, accepted27May2026. Data collected May2024.
source.verification_method: All supplied pages read; title, authors, DOI, dates, design and tables checked. Figure5/Table9 visually inspected. Crossref separately verifies cited GAToRS metadata, not its primary findings.

citation.title: Comfortably Numb: Uncanny Valley Effects are Not Present in Low-Stakes Patient Autonomy Dilemmas in Healthcare

reading.source_scope_note: Human online vignette evaluations under three pictured nurse types and two medication decisions. No actual care, patient triage, measured human-distinctiveness threat or manipulation of high versus low stakes.
access_limits: All20 extracted pages read, including all scales, model-selection procedure, tables, applications and references. Pages19/20 were read again separately after a truncated extraction. Figure5/Table9 on page14 visually inspected.

OSF raw data, analysis code, exact contrast coding, centering and selected-model sensitivity output were not independently reproduced. Original cited distinctiveness-threat, category-competition, speciesism and GAToRS primary studies remain unread.
The paper's clinical allocation advice and no-valley/high-stakes-only conclusions are not adopted as verified clinical or universal psychological findings.

study.sample: 540 UK native-English Prolific respondents, mean age34.7;5 fail both attention checks,535analyzed. £0.70 for approximately7minutes. One vignette per person; random assignment to6cells.
study.design: 3between-person agent conditions:human/android/mechanical nurse x2decisions:coercive medication/respect refusal. One image per agent, adapted from earlier studies.
study.outcomes: 10-item moral acceptability,1-item responsibility,3-item warmth,6-item competence,3-item trustworthiness. GAToRS20items measured after these judgments,4subscales used as covariates. Harm/fairness covariates removed for lowalpha.45/.36.
study.analysis: Separate regressions per outcome, agent-by-decision and selected agent-by-attitude interactions. Forward interaction selection using model-comparisonalpha.2. Initial unadjusted family thenalpha.01 across5outcomes; pairwise comparisonsTukey and additional threshold.0033.
study.results: No detected android/mechanical difference across outcomes. Stronger human advantage for warmth and responsibility; moral approval/competence/trust comparisons depend on conditioning and multiplicity. Respecting refusal improves moral approval, warmth and responsibility.
study.preferences: 88.4%prefer human nurse,4.7%android,6.9%mechanical.63.2%would respect refusal as nurse;74.8%want refusal respected as patient. These are hypothetical responses, not actual clinician/patient behavior.
study.interpretive_limit: Only one purportedly low-stakes vignette and no measured threat, eeriness or high-stakes comparison. Null detection does not prove equivalence, a missing effect everywhere or a necessary high-stakes condition.

summary: Add human-distinctiveness threat as an explicitly secondary, untested explanation. Supply a third fully read moral-uncanny-valley source with an informative null and a third agent-judgment-asymmetry source. Distinguish subjective evaluations from patient outcomes and avoid treating post-vignette attitudes as verified pre-existing causes.

findings.definition: A perceived challenge to attributes regarded as uniquely human that threatens a person's sense of human identity or distinctiveness.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Explicit secondary explanatory hypothesis in a fully read human study; not directly measured or causally tested in its own experiment
findings.ai_proposal: Investigate whether descriptions of an AI's capabilities lead people to feel that valued human qualities or roles are being undermined, using direct measures rather than assuming this from disagreement or discomfort. Distinguish identity concerns from evidence-based capability judgments and legitimate institutional concerns.
findings.novelty_rationale: A potential identity-related process, distinct from difficulty classifying an ambiguous stimulus, a generic dislike of robots, or self-humanization's aim of affirming one's own humanness. It is an explanation under study, not a demonstrated cause of every uncanny response.

evidence.quote: in turn erodes senses of personal identity and humanness.

findings.evidence_scope: The introduction summarizes hypotheses from cited literature; the discussion invokes weaker threat to explain a null android penalty. No identity-threat scale or manipulation discriminates this account from others in the535-person study.
findings.boundary: Feeling threatened, actual loss of human worth, task displacement, ambiguity and objectively demonstrated AI capability are distinct. Nonhuman entities having capabilities does not diminish human rights. No felt threat, human identity or conscious motive in an AI is inferred.

findings.definition: An appearance-related dip in approval of a robot's moral decisions; the present study does not detect the predicted android-versus-mechanical penalty.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing entry, now with a third fully read relevant article including a non-detection. Do not create an independent reverse-valley or low-stakes-no-valley behavior from each direction or null.

findings.evidence_scope: Three agent images and a single nursing vignette yield no detected android/mechanical contrast across five outcomes, with and reportedly without GAToRS adjustment. This is a contextual non-detection, not an equivalence or high-versus-low-stakes experiment.
findings.boundary: Null contrasts do not show the effect is absent in all patient-autonomy settings or requires high stakes. Contemporary eeriness/human-likeness and perceived stakes were not measured; prior image validation does not prove every participant saw an uncanny android.

findings.definition: Difficulty categorizing an almost familiar entity between categories, proposed to be effortful and generate negative affect.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing hypothesis, defined secondarily here rather than newly discovered. Distinguish it from identity threat and from an observed valley.

findings.evidence_scope: The introduction explicitly summarizes the stimulus-category competition account. Classification time, inhibition, effort and negative affect are not measured as its process indicators in the current experiment.
findings.boundary: This is a second fully read secondary theoretical source, not a second direct primary experiment or proof that categorization caused an AI-response effect. Legitimate ambiguity is not inherently a defect.

findings.definition: Human evaluations of moral decisions differ with whether the pictured nurse is human or robotic, with some contrasts not detected.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing agent-source pattern, here extending the evidence with a partly nonreplicating nursing result and separate approval/responsibility/trait outcomes.

findings.evidence_scope: Human nurses receive stronger warmth/responsibility judgments, but moral-approval and competence pairwise contrasts are not detected. The additional robot penalty for forced medication does not survive the five-outcome correction; covariate exclusion reportedly changes significance.
findings.boundary: Approval, responsibility, warmth, competence, trust and caregiver choice are different measures. A nominal conditional agent coefficient is not automatically a population-average human advantage; an undetected interaction does not prove identical effects. No actual robot moral action or universal double standard is established.

methodological_limits: Only one vignette is used. A three-image between-person contrast tests these pictured agents in this scenario; it does not estimate a continuous human-likeness curve, all medical dilemmas or a universal absence of moral uncanny valleys.

High versus low stakes are not randomized, and perceived stakes are not directly measured. Differences from separate trolley studies can reflect populations, stimuli, wording, analysis and context. The title/abstract's high-stakes-only implication is stronger than this design establishes.

The paper defines a broad uncorrected testing stage as a test for absence. Failure to reject effects, even under lenient thresholds, is not equivalence. Power for a chosenf does not establish every smaller effect is absent.

The five outcomes are correlated, not independent psychological replications. The two-stage familywise strategy is disclosed and should be retained; nominal results that fail its stricter threshold are not equally robust.

GAToRS is measured after the assigned vignette and moral/trait judgments. Treating it as 'pre-existing' without a baseline is not established, and adjustment may condition on post-treatment responses rather than isolate prior attitudes.

Forward model selection uses the same data, correlation ordering and an interaction inclusion threshold of.2. Subsequent selected-model p-values and subgroup slopes need appropriate uncertainty/validation; this is not proof the selected model is universally optimal.

Agent effects interact with attitude scores. If entered uncentered on their1–7scale, nominal agent coefficients apply at an outside-scale zero, not at an average respondent. Exact coding/centering is in unread code; conditional coefficients and marginal pairwise comparisons need separate interpretation.

Table6 mechanical-versus-android by decision listsbeta.43,SE.18,t1.94, which are not mutually consistent under ordinary coefficient/SE calculation. Table9P-minus listsbeta.02,SE.50,t.37, likewise inconsistent; rounding alone cannot explain that discrepancy. No corrected values are guessed.

Cross-sectional warmth/trust/approval mediation does not establish that increasing warmth or trust causes greater moral acceptance, or that agent type acts only through those mediators. Mediators are not randomized and can share evaluative content.

Figure5 shows one agent path despite a three-level factor; its exact contrast or numeric coding is not explained in the supplied mediation text. Itsc/c-prime labels and negative indirect paths require reconciliation with the prose's significant-before/non-significant-after description before causal interpretation.

The printed trust indirect interval ends at.00 while the prose calls it significant. More precision is needed to establish whether its actual interval excludes zero; rounding is not proof of an error or of significance.

Moral acceptability text is reused in the responsibility results. Lower responsibility is not identical to lower approval, and a person can be judged responsible for an act without it being blameworthy.

The medication instruction is called imperative by the physician but not absolutely indispensable by the nurse's experience/database. The vignette bundles authority obedience, autonomy, necessity and medical beliefs; it does not establish objectively appropriate treatment.

Forced medication's physical versus mental coercion, capacity, diagnosis and consent are unspecified. Calling the scenario low stakes does not establish coercion is clinically minor or ethically permissible.

The sample is online UK adults responding hypothetically, not patients receiving robot care. No treatment outcomes, real patient experience, diagnostic discrimination, predictive calibration or external clinical validation of GAToRS triage is tested.

The clinical recommendation to assign robot practitioners based on highGAToRS scores exceeds these data. Correlations do not establish a diagnostic tool, and claiming dishonest patients will manipulate scores is not observed in this study.

Warmth, competence and trust can correlate with approval without the underlying act becoming safer or morally right. Improving perceptions is not a substitute for justified treatment, consent or clinical governance.

Thoughtful free text, platform reputation and a90% approval filter support quality control but do not prove every response is human-generated or uninfluenced by an LLM. Conversely, no AI use is established by the supplied evidence.

The study has no in-sample human-likeness/eeriness check, although images have prior validation. Prior validation plus a null moral contrast does not establish the sensory uncanny response was absent here.

Source interpretations that deontology never trades lives, that robots need human-like feeling to judge morality, or that one culture uniformly values autonomy less are theoretical generalizations, not new experimental findings.

cross_paper_learning.finding: The2023 appearance study reports decision-dependent valley/reversal patterns. This null nursing contrast adds useful scope evidence but does not directly test stakes as a moderator or erase the earlier variation by decision.
Provides another explicit definition of stimulus-category competition, while neither paper directly identifies the proposed classification/inhibition process as the source of moral judgments.

The earlier forced-medication experiments detect a robot-by-decision pattern. Here that extra penalty depends on covariate inclusion and multiplicity. Treat it as a qualified or nonreplicating finding, not universal equality or proof that general attitudes causally explain the earlier result.

Experience attribution is a human belief about feeling, not proof of machine experience. Here human-distinctiveness threat is proposed but unmeasured, and future clinical allocation is not validated by a vignette preference.

Statistical mediation remains an associational account unless mediator-outcome assumptions hold. Null differences do not prove elimination, and hypothetical preferences do not establish real patient or buying behavior.

deferred.reason: The source gives a secondary, narrow gloss about human moral superiority and cites a medical-AI study. Its full distinction between species-based moral standing, agency beliefs and justified capability differences needs primary reading before a new entry.
A null or reversed outcome is not automatically another independent mechanism. Preserve it as qualified evidence on the existing entry.

deferred.term: GAToRS as a behavioral defect or validated clinical diagnostic
deferred.reason: A20-item attitude instrument, not a new failure mode. Its clinical allocation validity is not tested here.

deferred.term: Moral status differences explained entirely by prior attitudes
deferred.reason: Post-vignette covariates, selected interactions and changed significance do not identify that causal explanation.

deferred.term: Equivalence of all nurse types or proof that high stakes are necessary
deferred.reason: No equivalence margin or direct stakes manipulation establishes either conclusion.

limitations: One secondary explanatory concept is added, not a proven human or AI mechanism. Existing constructs gain a relevant null and replication limits. No clinical triage rule, machine subjective state, unread-primary quota, ethical edge or annual count is invented.
